subject: Follow-up: hosting SLA, procurement checklist, and next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.p@medisync.ai>, Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@medisync.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: hosting SLA, procurement checklist, and next steps

Hi Asha / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we agreed on so procurement/legal have clarity:

What Medisync told us today
- Primary decision criteria: predictable unit cost and p95 inference latency under load.
- Hosting preference: VPC/private deployment is preferred but dedicated-hosted option is acceptable if controls match.
- Security gating: SOC 2 Type II evidence, penetration test summary, and a DPA will be required before procurement signoff.

Clarifying targets we heard in the meeting
- Latency: target p95 <= 200ms for short requests (avg 128 tokens). We should plan for higher tail under peak.
- Cost: target per-1k-token equivalent aim to be within your budget envelope (you mentioned wanting to stay within ~ $0.50–$1.50 per 1k prompt+completion units depending on batching).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime expectation with a numeric credit schedule for major outages (your procurement said a written SLA must be in the quote).

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses)
- Vanessa: send a concise procurement packet (SOC2 summary, draft quote, SOW outline, high-level architecture). Attached: meeting recording + draft quote + SOW stub.
- Neha (cc): confirm which security artifacts we can provide publicly and which require an NDA.
- Sam / Procurement: share the procurement questionnaire or legal redlines and any internal vendor onboarding steps.

Proposed timeline
- Week of 7/19: share procurement questionnaire / draft DPA requests.
- 7/22: procurement + security sync (30–45m) to walk artifacts and clarify SLA credits.

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the 7/22 slot and prep the packet with Neha and Marcus.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187
Redwood Inference

Attachments: meeting_recording_20270714.mp4, draft_quote_2027-07-14.pdf, redwood_sow_v1.pdf
From: Asha Patel <asha.p@medisync.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medisync.ai, Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@medisync.ai>
Date: 2027-07-14T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting SLA, procurement checklist, and next steps

Hi Vanessa —

Appreciate the recap. This matches our notes. A few items procurement/legal need to proceed:

1) Security artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report (or summary), pen test executive summary, and your DPA template. We can accept an attested SOC2 summary while legal completes vendor onboarding.

2) SLA language: procurement needs a draft SLA with uptime % and credit schedule. Please include RTO/RPO if you have planned runbooks for larger incidents.

3) Hosting variants: call out costs and controls for (a) Redwood-hosted dedicated, (b) Redwood Private VPC in our AWS account, and (c) on-prem (we may not choose on-prem but want the option noted). We need clear notes on data residency and access controls for each.

4) Finance: a ballpark ARR commitment and a quote for 12 months so we can evaluate against budget. Include any standard onboarding/one-time fees.

I’ll loop procurement@medisync.ai (internal vendor team). We’re available on 7/22 — please share a 30–45 minute invite with an agenda focused on security gating and SLA credits.

—asha
Asha Patel
Head of Product Ops | Medisync AI
asha.p@medisync.ai

Quoted from meeting: “we need an SLA we can present to legal that includes measurable credits — otherwise procurement will push for a longer evaluation period.”
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-15T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: hosting SLA, procurement checklist, and next steps

Vanessa / Marcus —

I reviewed Asha’s requests. We can put together the following package for the 7/22 procurement call:

- SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted) and an internal controls checklist.
- Pen test executive summary (non-sensitive findings only).
- Draft DPA + standard security addendum template.
- High-level architecture diagram showing data flow, KV cache handling, and where encryption-at-rest/in-transit is enforced.
- Hosting matrix (Dedicated vs Private VPC vs On-prem): security controls and expected variance in per-token economics + estimated p95 under typical batch sizes.
- Proposed SLA language (99.9% uptime, outage definitions, credits tiers). Marcus: can you draft the numeric credit schedule and a short paragraph on incident response / escalation?

I need to know which artifacts we can share pre-NDA. If Medisync insists on full SOC 2 report under NDA only, we should prepare the redacted summary to keep momentum.

I’ll assemble the Drive folder with those docs and share a single link today. Vanessa, please confirm whether we should add our standard vendor questionnaire or wait for theirs.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
